# Actual-service validation through the real consumer network

The runtime test links the retained original save and guarded UI caller transfers,
their ordinary-C implementations, and the existing complete generated cleanup
machine/logical adapters. Dynamic text and scratch origins use the actual native
issuer, resolver, realization and release bodies. Consumer views use generated
production access helpers. The generated logical cleanup adapter is invoked with
its own actual service-context structure; its fault flags are observed explicitly.

Fifteen cases run on both sides (30 executions). Real PE32/Wine GlobalAlloc,
GlobalFree, lstrlenA, lstrcpyA, SetFocus and SendMessageA operate on two actual EDIT
windows. An EDIT subclass forwards replacement to the original window procedure,
records the delivered text, and returns selected 32-bit values including
UINT32_MAX and 0x80000000. Its focus callback can update the image's edit handle,
exercising the caller's required post-cleanup read. This is an actual synchronous
callback in the fixture, not general callback or UI-runtime qualification.

Cases cover both bypass modes, unsigned mode and length boundaries, one/two CRCRLF
removals, empty/short text, injected allocation failure with empty/nonempty text,
interior text references, input prefix/suffix guards, live input aliases, expired
scratch origins, owner-release expiry, normal continuation stack/register values,
and exact ordered service/fault prefixes. UI delivery checks a terminator inside
the current live extent; pointer reconstruction alone never supplies this fact.
After delivery, mutating the borrowed input and then releasing its owner must
leave the EDIT control's copied contents unchanged.

The image bytes are the retained original `metapad.exe` (194,560 bytes; SHA256
`685989bad8d8119eddbb49e36006d8ac9155c45d69dee060807368241c8e58ce`), copied from
`build/metapad-trial/metapad.exe`. This identity matches the existing image authority
and retained original module interface. Windows SEC_IMAGE mapping uses the actual
PE sections, with LoadStringA reading its original resource 31. Its entry point is
not invoked. The resource supplier is the exact ordinary C from the public normal and loop-edit
proof products, called through its generated logical adapter in a separate
translation unit. `resource-text.c` (SHA256
`6ff797884212a58148b4442effa4c1923ac3d13a3864f134d66b81b002fce54f`) and
`resource-text-loop.c` (SHA256
`d054db6b8aade7c6301402e878e2f0da0447f9e4a8ae801071ac9d4705744b4b`) come from
`practical-assurance/cleanup-tail-suppliers-v1/{normal,loop-edit}/material/source/sources/`.
Both implementations run the complete 30-execution fixture; their generated
interface headers also match the public proof dependencies.

Wine reserves the preferred original address before main. The fixture translates
retained image addresses to the actual mapped base for memory access and resolution,
and translates realized image references back to retained coordinates. The native
context records the actual base/extent; the production image locator, resolver and
realizer handle all four original image origins alongside the dynamic allocator.
Resource coordinates and native-to-retained transport are checked explicitly.
This translation and raw memory admission are fixture-owned; they do not qualify a
general relocation/loader adapter. Stack admission also remains fixture-owned.

Each run resets only the writable original data section, installs the actual image
handle and selects the length-service IAT word under restored page protection.
Caption bytes remain in the original read-only section. Notice cases for both
consumers call actual MessageBoxA, checking its text, caption, flags, return and
ordered resource/message/focus effects. A thread-local CBT hook observes only dialog
activation and posts IDOK to the fixture's own dialog. Resource success/termination
is observed for this real resource; no arbitrary LoadString failure or termination
promise is inferred. Unmapping the image and removing its native admission rejects
the saved resource reference. Same-base unload/reload generations are not qualified.

The EDIT subclass chooses reply values; these are
not claimed to be the default EDIT control's replies. Original caller reachability,
arbitrary service invocation failures, nonreturn, callbacks beyond the tested
focus update, and complete native activation remain unqualified. Allocation failure
is injected here; retained allocation-contract tests cover actual maximum-width
Win32 failure separately.

This is finite runtime validation, separate from the rigorous conditional local
proofs and their public contract/edit/reuse workflow. It creates no proof or
activation receipt. Negative controls break current-handle ordering, release
registration, text generation, count arithmetic, a mode guard, caption origin, resource contents and missing image-admission removal.
